name: joystick_deflection_minimum
label: Joystick center dead zone
description: Center dead zone for the analog stick, as a percent of full travel. Set it high enough to stop a wandering mouse or joystick. This is a separate thing from the D-Pad rings. On firmware 2373 a value of 0 no longer means no dead zone: the device substitutes 129 raw counts instead, and it redoes that on every scan, so it wins over the value worked out when the file was loaded.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py slider_NEUTRAL (0..20) and its tooltip; qsflash.py defaults '8'. Firmware 2373 Preferences.h:97 also defaults to 8, and DataFlow.c:997 is where 0 becomes 129 raw counts, overriding Configuration.c:376.

name: joystick_deflection_maximum

description: How far the stick has to move for a full signal. QMP takes the largest of its four direction sliders.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py slider_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT (10..50) and calculate_joystick_preferences; qsflash.py defaults '25'

name: deflection_multiplier_up
label: Up deflection multiplier
description: Scales the up direction so it reaches a full signal at the same point as the other directions.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py calculate_joystick_preferences computes max*100/slider, so it has no fixed range; qsflash.py defaults '140'

name: deflection_multiplier_down
label: Down deflection multiplier
description: Scales the down direction so it reaches a full signal at the same point as the other directions.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py calculate_joystick_preferences computes max*100/slider, so it has no fixed range; qsflash.py defaults '130'

name: deflection_multiplier_left

source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py calculate_joystick_preferences computes max*100/slider, so it has no fixed range; qsflash.py defaults '100'

name: deflection_multiplier_right

name: joystick_D_Pad_inner
label: Inner D-Pad ring
description: Percent of full deflection, measured from the center, where the inner D-Pad ring starts. It only fires after a short delay, so you can move through it on the way out without triggering it. Half this value is where a direction stops being held.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py slider_D_Pad_inner_ring (10..100) and its tooltip; qsflash.py defaults '25'. Firmware 2373 Configuration.c:367-372 converts it with (value * 1023) / 100, so it is a percent of full deflection from the center, and takes half of it as the release threshold. Preferences.h:101 also defaults to 25.

name: joystick_D_Pad_outer
label: Outer D-Pad ring
description: Percent of full deflection, measured from the center, where the outer D-Pad ring starts. Past this line a direction fires straight away.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py slider_D_Pad_outer_ring (10..100) and its tooltip; qsflash.py defaults '80'. Firmware 2373 Configuration.c:367-372 converts it with (value * 1023) / 100, so it is a percent of full deflection from the center. The device's own default is 65 (Preferences.h:102), which is what it uses when a file leaves this out; 80 is what QMP-4 writes.

name: sip_threshold_soft

source: QuadStick Google Group, Fred Davison, 2026-08-09, announcing the firmware that splits sip from puff: six new preferences, all default 0, 0 means the matching sip_puff_* setting is in effect. Percent and the default are his; the 0..100 bounds are the unit's own scale. Firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h carries all six and DataFlow.c:290-317 confirms both halves of that: each one is used only when it is not zero, and it scales with the same (value * range) / 100 expression as the combined setting, so the percent means the same thing. name: enable_usb_a_device
label: USB-A device mode
risk: This picks which USB port the QuadStick presents itself on. The device tears USB down and reconnects when it changes, so a wrong value can leave it unseen by a console or computer. It also beats enable_usb_a_host: while this is set, the USB-A host stack is shut down whatever the host setting says. Change it only on advice from QuadStick support.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h ENABLE_USB_A_DEVICE, passed to USB_Init and USB_Connect in Joystick.c:599 and :630 and Configuration.c:354-357, and checked first in JoystickHost.c:590. Preferences.h:134 defaults to 0. QMP-4 QuadStick.py writes the separate enable_usb_a_host instead.

name: enable_usb_a_host
label: USB-A host mode
description: Since firmware 2373. With this on and USB-A device mode off, the device runs a USB host on the USB-A port, so a controller plugged in there feeds the usb_1 input channels. Turn it off, or turn USB-A device mode on, and the host is torn down. USB-A device mode wins.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h ENABLE_USB_A_HOST; Preferences.h:135 defaults to 1. JoystickHost.c:590 is the only read: the host is de-enumerated when enable_usb_a_device is set or this one is clear. Firmware 1476 has no such keyword, though QMP-4 QuadStick.py already wrote the name.

name: enable_DS3_emulation
label: USB emulation mode
description: Which USB device the QuadStick pretends to be. On firmware 2373: 0 QuadStick native, 1 DualShock 3, 2 x360ce, 3 Xbox 360, 4 DualShock 4 for a PS4, 5 Nintendo Switch Pro Controller, 6 DualShock 4 with no USB drive, 7 straight DS4 wireless. Value 5 meant PC only, no joystick on firmware 1476, so a file carrying 5 behaves completely differently once the device is updated.
risk: The name says DS3, but the device reads it as a USB emulation mode with eight numbered values, not an on or off switch. What 5 means changed between firmware 1476 and 2373, and a number the running firmware does not know leaves the device on an emulation nobody asked for. QCM keeps whatever is typed and refuses nothing, because a value that is wrong for one firmware is right for another. Change it only on advice from QuadStick support.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h maps it to USB_EMULATION_MODE; Descriptors.c:1292 switches on all eight values, DescriptorsDS4.c:803 and :807 tell 6 (no USB drive) from 7 (straight DS4 wireless), and Joystick.c and DataFlow.c switch on the same numbers. Firmware 1476 Descriptors.c:1523 had 5 as PC only, no joystick. Preferences.h:138 defaults to 0. QMP-4 QuadStick.py checkbox_ps4_boot_mode treats it as a checkbox.

name: usb_1_dead_zone
label: USB 1 dead zone
description: Since firmware 2373. Center dead zone for a controller plugged into the USB-A host port, counted in raw steps of that controller's centered axis byte, not in percent. Under the value the axis reads 0; over it the value is taken off so travel starts from zero, and the result is held to plus or minus 100. At 0 the axis passes through untouched. A centered axis byte only reaches about 127 either way, so 128 or more kills the axis.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h USB_1_DEAD_ZONE; Preferences.h:132 defaults to 20. JoystickHost.c:242-250 is the subtractive dead zone, fed the axis bytes with 128 taken off at :354-357, :374-377, :481-482 and :500-503, and written out again at :304-311 and :329-336. No source states a range, so none is claimed here.

name: usb_2_dead_zone
label: USB 2 dead zone
description: Since firmware 2373, but the device ignores it. The name is legal and files carry it, yet nothing in the firmware reads the value: every USB host axis uses the USB 1 dead zone. Setting it in a mode row does nothing either.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h USB_2_DEAD_ZONE; Preferences.h:133 defaults to 20. That line, the Preferences.h:60 enum entry, the keyword table and the Configuration.c:153 default table are the only four places the name appears in the firmware tree, so nothing reads it.

name: titan_two
label: Titan Two adapter
description: Since firmware 2373. Tells the device it is reaching a PS4 through a Titan Two rather than plugged straight into the console. It then skips the DS4 authentication handshake and stops the periodic forced USB reconnect.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h TITAN_TWO; Preferences.h:146 defaults to 0. JoystickHost.c:570 skips the DS4 authentication state machine when it is set, and Joystick.c:862 and DataFlow.c:2842 both zero the PS4 reset timer. The firmware's own comment at Joystick.c:862 says a T2 makes the QuadStick think it is directly connected to a PS4 when it is not, so that reset is never needed.

name: watchdog_disable
label: Disable the watchdog
risk: The device runs a two minute hardware watchdog that restarts it if it stops responding. Nothing in firmware 1476 or 2373 reads this setting, so on either one it does nothing, and what a later firmware might do with it is unknown.
source: QMP-4 qsflash.py defaults '0'; firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h DISABLE_WATCHDOG, with the two minute watchdog set up in Joystick.c:569-573. Preferences.h:111 defaults to 0. The keyword table, the enum, the default macro and the Configuration.c:131 default table are the only places the name appears.
